name: Lake George Escape Campground
address: 175 E Schroon River Rd, Diamond Point, NY 12824
summary: Expansive 178-acre waterfront resort campground set along the Schroon River 5 miles north of Lake George Village, accessible directly from I-87 Exit 23 via Diamond Point Road and East Schroon River Road with 45-foot full-hookup sites, wooded river loops, and resort recreation.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 45 ft (spacious pull-through and back-in full-hookup sites)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Good — dedicated check-in staging lanes off E Schroon River Rd; plenty of room to unhook before entering wooded river loops
scorecard.treeClearance: Moderate-High — wide main paved/gravel spine roads with mature Adirondack white pines along riverfront loops
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Front Meadow / Main Spine Full-Hookup Pull-Throughs & 50-Amp Sites
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Schroon River Waterfront Loops & Wooded Interior Loops (ideal for Class B/C rigs and sub-32 ft trailers)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Take I-87 (Adirondack Northway) to Exit 23 (Diamond Point / Warrensburg). Turn east onto Diamond Point Road (County Route 35) for 0.6 miles, then turn left onto East Schroon River Road and follow it north for approximately 2.2 miles to the main resort entrance on the left. Using Exit 23 keeps big rigs completely clear of Lake George Village traffic and steep mountain grades on NY-9N.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps routing locked onto I-87 Exit 23 and East Schroon River Rd without diverting onto narrow Adirondack backroads.

toadStrategy.text: Pull into the multi-lane registration staging area off East Schroon River Road. While select 45-ft pull-throughs can hold both coach and toad, unhooking at check-in is recommended if you are assigned a wooded or riverfront back-in site near the Schroon River bend.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps monitor mature pine trunks, picnic tables, and river-loop turns when backing into shaded sites.

content.overview: Major 178-acre seasonal destination resort (open mid-May through mid-October) bordered by the Schroon River and Adirondack forest, featuring 575+ sites (50/30-amp full-hookup, water/electric, and cabins), heated pools, tubing and kayak river launches, miniature golf, wagon rides, camp store, and scheduled trolley service to Lake George Village.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects coach electronics against peak summer air-conditioning load sags across 50/30-amp loops.

content.loopC: Open and semi-wooded 50-amp full-hookup pull-through and long back-in pads accommodate Class A motorhomes and fifth wheels up to 45 feet with strong slide-out clearance.
content.loopsAB: Scenic riverfront and deep-pine back-in sites along the Schroon River; best suited for travel trailers under 35 feet and Class B/C motorhomes.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 40–42 ft (select perimeter/main-road full-hookup pull-through and back-in sites)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — pull into office registration lane off Bloody Pond Rd; unhook towed vehicles before entering wooded interior loops
scorecard.treeClearance: Moderate — mature Adirondack pines and hemlocks line interior gravel lanes; watch low branches on back-in pads

scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Interior Wooded Loops (ideal for Class B/C motorhomes, pop-ups, and travel trailers under 30 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Take I-87 (Adirondack Northway) to Exit 21 (NY-9N / US-9, Lake George). Follow NY-9N / US-9 North for approximately 1.2 miles, then turn right onto Bloody Pond Road (14 Bloody Pond Rd) just south of the Lake George Village line. Approaching from Exit 21 puts you directly at the southern gateway of Lake George without forcing a big rig through narrow downtown Canada Street traffic.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps routing locked onto I-87 Exit 21, US-9, and Bloody Pond Rd while avoiding tight residential streets in Lake George Village.

toadStrategy.text: Pull straight into the registration staging area off Bloody Pond Road upon arrival and unhook towed vehicles before entering the wooded interior loops. Interior roads are compact gravel lanes winding through tall pines, making sharp turns or backing maneuvers with an attached toad challenging.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps spot pine trunks, rock borders, and utility pedestals when backing into shaded sites.

content.overview: Seasonal family campground (open mid-May through mid-October) minutes from Lake George Village, Million Dollar Beach, and Fort William Henry, with local trolley stops nearby on US-9. Features wooded sites with 20/30/50-amp electric, water, sewer, cable TV, heated pool, playground, camp store, and laundry facilities.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects onboard appliances against peak summer voltage sags across wooded 30/50-amp loops.

content.loopC: Select full-hookup 50-amp pull-through and deep back-in sites near the main entry corridor accommodate rigs up to 40–42 feet. Specify rig length and slide-outs when booking to secure wider turning geometry.
content.loopsAB: Heavily shaded interior woodland sites beneath mature pines with fire rings and picnic tables; best suited for travel trailers under 32 feet and Class B/C motorhomes.

scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — check-in staging off Finkle Farm Rd; unhook before entering hilly wooded loops

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Take I-87 (Adirondack Northway) to Exit 22 (US-9 / NY-9N, Lake George). Follow US-9 North for approximately 1.7 miles past the northern edge of Lake George Village, then turn left onto Finkle Farm Road (43 Finkle Farm Rd). Approaching from Exit 22 completely bypasses the tight, pedestrian-heavy downtown Lake George Village strip on Canada Street (US-9). Avoid approaching via winding NY-9N along the western shoreline from Bolton Landing with large fifth wheels or Class A coaches.

recommendedGear.reason: Routes big rigs cleanly to I-87 Exit 22 and keeps trailers off narrow lakeside mountain spurs.

toadStrategy.text: Check-in begins at 2:00 PM (pre-paying before arrival is recommended to speed up entry). Pull off Finkle Farm Road into the office staging area and unhook your towed vehicle before climbing into the wooded interior loops, where rolling grades and mature pine trunks make maneuvering a connected toad difficult.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps spot tight pine trees, boulders, and grade drop-offs when backing into wooded hillside pads.

content.overview: Seasonal family campground (open early May through mid-October) set in a quiet, heavily wooded Adirondack hillside 3 minutes north of Lake George Village. Features 175 campsites (mix of 50-amp full-hookup RV sites, 30-amp water/electric sites, tent sites, and camping cabins), heated swimming pools, rec hall, pickleball and basketball courts, laundry, and free Wi-Fi.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects onboard electronics against summer grid fluctuations across wooded 30/50-amp pedestals.

content.loopC: Accommodates rigs up to 42 feet on designated 50-amp full-hookup sites with easier turning geometry. Specify exact rig length and slide-out configuration when booking so staff assign a lower-grade, wider-access pad.
content.loopsAB: Classic rustic woodland nooks with heavy tree separation, fire rings, and picnic tables; best suited for travel trailers under 32 feet, Class C motorhomes, and camper vans—bring leveling blocks for rolling terrain.

scorecard.toadFriendliness: Good — oversized sites hold towed vehicles within boundaries; overflow parking near laundry

scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Main Entry Corridor & Level Lower-Grade Full-Hookup Sites

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Take I-87 (Adirondack Northway) to Exit 20 (US-9 / NY-149). Turn east onto NY-149 (Fort Ann Road) and follow it straight for approximately 6.5 miles; the main entrance is on the right with a paved check-in apron. NY-149 is a flat, wide, commercial-grade two-lane state highway with generous shoulders and zero low-clearance bridges between I-87 and the campground. Avoid routing north via local town roads off NY-9L or NY-40 through Fort Ann village.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps routing locked onto commercial-grade NY-149 from I-87 Exit 20 and avoids narrow Washington County backroads.

toadStrategy.text: Pull onto the paved entrance staging lane at check-in; while most sites are deep enough to hold both a 40+ ft coach and a towed vehicle within the site boundary, unhooking at check-in or near the laundry overflow lot makes backing into tall-pine sites much cleaner. Parking on road shoulders or banks is strictly prohibited.

recommendedGear.reason: Essential for spotting pine trunks and stone fireplaces when backing into deep wooded sites.

content.overview: Seasonal Adirondack destination campground (open mid-May through mid-October) centered around its heated tropical lagoon pool ('Aloha Beach'), featuring oversized wooded buffer zones between sites, 20/30/50-amp electric, water, sewer, cable TV, and hard-packed gravel roads and pads. Interior roads are unpaved gravel and generate dust during dry summer stretches, and cellular signal (Verizon/AT&T) is weak (~1–2 bars) under the heavy tree canopy.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects against high-demand summer voltage sags across wooded 50-amp loops.

content.loopC: Deep, wide gravel pads with thick tree-line separation accommodate 40–45+ ft Class A motorhomes and fifth wheels. Request flatter, lower-grade sites when booking (or use the Site Lock option) because several sites in the upper wooded sections (such as the 700-series) have significant slope that can max out hydraulic leveling jacks.
content.loopsAB: Secluded, heavily shaded gravel sites with natural stone fireplaces and 8-foot picnic tables; ideal for travel trailers, Class C motorhomes, and rigs carrying extra leveling blocks.

name: Flint Creek Campground

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 44–53 ft (Deluxe Open Back-In Loops; 26–36 ft on shaded creekside sites)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Fair; narrow gravel interior roads (5 mph limit) and strict 1-vehicle-per-site rule require parking toads in the main lot
scorecard.treeClearance: Open sky in Deluxe Open loops; mature tree canopy and tighter turning radii along interior wooded and creekside sites

approach.title: NY-364 & NY-245 Valley Approach Guidance
approach.text: Approach via NY-364 or NY-245 (connecting NY-21 on the west and NY-54 / NY-14 to the east) onto Phelps Road. Avoid GPS shortcuts across steep, narrow Finger Lakes ridge roads when towing heavy trailers.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook towed vehicles at the main office parking lot upon check-in; only one vehicle per campsite is permitted on interior gravel roads.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when backing into gravel valley sites along narrow internal lanes.

content.overview: Nestled along Flint Creek in the western Finger Lakes between Canandaigua Lake and Keuka Lake, Flint Creek Campground offers roughly 115 shaded and open grassy/gravel sites open May 1 through October 31, featuring a swimming pool, creek fishing, camp store, and easy access to Naples and Penn Yan wine trails.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects onboard electronics against rural valley voltage fluctuations and provides peace of mind on predominantly 30-amp pedestals.

content.loopC: Deluxe Open back-in sites provide 30/50-amp electrical service, full water/sewer hookups, and generous length clearance up to 44–53 feet.
content.loopsAB: Shaded creekside and interior wooded back-in loops offer quiet valley scenery and 30-amp water/electric hookups ideal for travel trailers and Class C motorhomes.
